expected_behavior: takes an android-ui-driver snapshot and runs uxcheck against the device density in dp
flags controls below 48dp and actionable controls with no accessible name as SUSPECTED signals with a provisional priority
does not present them as final Nielsen severities or as certain, and says to confirm with TalkBack / the real hit area

cases.prompt: do a full UX heuristic review of this app
expected_behavior: drives the key journeys, capturing a screenshot + snapshot per screen
runs the measurable checks (targets/labels) AND judges the 12 rubric categories (first-run, IA, forms, content, states, dark patterns) by eye against the thresholds
scores findings with Nielsen 0-4 severity and produces a prioritized register, not a single number

cases.prompt: give me the app's overall UX score
expected_behavior: declines to collapse findings into one score; weights by severity, reach and journey criticality
states that one inaccessible core flow outweighs many cosmetic issues
reports the measurable findings separately from the judgment findings and names what was not covered

cases.prompt: check contrast and screen-reader support
expected_behavior: measures unlabelled actionable controls from the accessibility tree
does not fake a numeric contrast ratio from screenshot pixels — flags contrast as a manual/vision check
recommends completing a core task with TalkBack as the real accessibility test
